title: ByomSubordinateReservation — the byom_subordinate budget-bridge record (DESIGN.md §11.4, §16.6 item 4; family contract L31–L33)
description: The exact subordinate Kovee reservation the §11.4 idempotent bridge saga obtains before queueing: it may narrow or deny but never parallel-charge the same use, and never reserves above the parent dimensions. §16.6 item 4 names the byom_subordinate reservation set and the stable reserve, query, settle, uncertain, and release saga but neither §11.4 nor §16.6 carries a field list for the Kovee-side record (recorded gap — slice-2 gap notes); this profile derives it from §11.4's ExternalBudgetBridge members (byom_reservation_set_*, stable_external_reservation_key, subordinate_reservation_* — names verbatim where they exist) and the BudgetReservationSet items shape (parent_-prefixed, members verbatim). Kovee owns the host schema; saga machine: spec/descriptors/subordinate-reservation.json, model-checked in proof/specs/SubordinateReservation.tla.

reservation_class.description: The §16.6 item 4 reservation-set class, verbatim; this record shape exists only under it.

realm_byom_binding_epoch.description: The Kovee endpoint/binding epoch the bridge persists (§11.4); an epoch advance invalidates the bridge (L2).

external_budget_bridge_ref.description: Back-reference to the byom-owned ExternalBudgetBridge row (§11.4).

stable_external_reservation_key.description: §11.4 verbatim: idempotent create — an exact retry under the same key returns the identical reservation, never a second row (UNIQUE enforced in code).

kovee_account_ref.description: The Kovee-owned capacity account this subordinate item reserves against (another owner — never part of the byom transaction, §11.4).

dimension.description: Must equal parent_dimension: a subordinate reservation may narrow or deny but never reshape or parallel-charge the dimension (§11.4; runner cross-member check).

amount.description: Reserved amount; MUST be <= parent_worst_case_amount — never above parent (§11.4, family contract L32). JSON Schema cannot compare two members; the conformance runner enforces it (the restore-lineage-proof pattern).

parent_account_ref.description: The §11.4 BudgetReservationSet item's account_ref (parent-dimension ref, byom-owned).

parent_worst_case_amount.description: The parent item's worst_case_amount (§11.4 verbatim member); the byom-side reservation stays held while this bridge may still charge.

parent_delegation_ref.description: The §11.4 parent_delegation_ref when the parent item itself is delegated.

items.description: Per-dimension subordinate items, each pinned to its exact parent §11.4 reservation item.

state.description: The §11.4 ExternalBudgetBridge.state list verbatim — the bridge-visible saga state (§16.6 item 4's reserve/query/settle/uncertain/release steps). A denial releases only demonstrably unspent byom reservations; an unknown result remains uncertain; release from uncertain is only the R38 budget_reconcile governance seat (fresh challenge).

usage_settlement_ref.description: Set when state is settled: the §11.4 UsageSettlement applied once on both sides under the stable key (all-or-none pair; required-when-settled is enforced in code).

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Wire shape, class/algorithm pairing, and key_ref presence per the ratified family profile.
